module purpose: Parameterized FIFO: accepts write data wdata_i under write enable we_i, stores entries in an internal single-word register or an array (fifo_reg / fifo_mem) addressed by write pointer w_pnt, provides read data on rdata_o selected by read pointer r_pnt (or r_pnt_ff for async read), and reports occupancy/status via level_o, free_o, avail_o and half_o. Supports optional synchronous read path, optional full-memory reset, and a clear input that zeros the pointers.

use-case flows.value: enqueue: accept wdata_i and store it into the FIFO memory/register and advance the write pointer
dequeue: select an entry from storage into rdata_o and advance the read pointer
report FIFO occupancy and status: compute level, half, full/empty-derived free/avail, and present them on level_o, half_o, free_o, avail_o (either directly or synchronized)
deliver stored entry value to an external consumer via rdata_o (async or sync path depending on FIFO_RSYNC and FIFO_DEPTH)
clear pointers and (when FULL_RESET) clear memory contents while rstn_i = '0'

conceptual assets.concept: Stored FIFO payloads (the data words placed into FIFO entries and later returned on read)
conceptual assets.reasoning: Writes place wdata_i into the FIFO register or memory under the write enable path and the write pointer and the written value is later selected onto rdata_o. The RTL shows next-pointer and write gating (w_nxt / we) and the actual write statements (e.g. fifo_reg <= wdata_i / fifo_mem(...) <= wdata_i at lines 135, 150, 171, 184) and read paths that select those storage locations onto rdata_o (lines 201, 213, 232, 241). The map records show the memories are clocked registers (fifo_reg and fifo_mem CLOCKED_BY clk_i at the write occurrences) and wdata_i drives those stores while rdata_o derives from the stored memory: this establishes the stored payload as an integrity-sensitive value delivered by this entity.

conceptual assets.concept: Pointer state (write pointer w_pnt, read pointer r_pnt and the async-read shadow r_pnt_ff) that determine which storage location is written or read
conceptual assets.reasoning: The FIFO's addressing and ordering are carried in w_pnt and r_pnt (reset to zero when rstn_i='0' in the pointer_reg process, lines 72-75) and updated on clk_i (w_pnt <= w_nxt, r_pnt <= r_nxt at lines 76-77). The pointers index fifo_mem for writes and reads (the writes use to_integer(unsigned(w_pnt(...))) at line 150/184 and the read selections use r_pnt or r_pnt_ff at lines 213/241). The map shows these elements are clocked registers (w_pnt and r_pnt CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 3, r_pnt_ff CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 2) and are used as selectors in the memory access records, so pointer integrity is established by the RTL.

conceptual assets.concept: Read / write commit decisions (the internal we and re signals computed from the external we_i / re_i and availability flags) that gate whether a write or read actually occurs
conceptual assets.reasoning: The module computes internal write/read enables from the external ports and the internal availability signals (re <= re_i or re_i and avail; we <= we_i or we_i and free, lines 64-65). Those internal enables gate pointer advancement and the memory/register write or read selection (see w_nxt/r_nxt lines 82-83 and the guarded memory assignments at lines 135,150,171,184 and selection at 213/241). The map shows the ports we_i/re_i are SOURCES for the internal decisions (we_i SOURCES we at occurrence 2 line 65; re_i SOURCES re at occurrence 2 line 64) and the internal we/re are DERIVES_FROM those inputs (we at occurrence 2 line 65, re at occurrence 2 line 64). Corrupting these decisions would change whether stores or reads occur, so their integrity is established.

conceptual assets.concept: Occupancy count (level) — the computed fill level exposed to consumers via level_o
conceptual assets.reasoning: The FIFO computes level as unsigned(w_pnt) - unsigned(r_pnt) (line 95) and then extends and presents that value on level_o (level_extend process, lines 114-117). The map shows level DERIVES_FROM the pointers at occurrence 2 line 95 and level_o DERIVES_FROM level at occurrence 3 line 117. Because external consumers receive level_o and may depend on it, the RTL establishes the occupancy count's integrity requirement.

conceptual assets.concept: Availability / fullness flags (free, avail, half) and their exported ports (free_o, avail_o, half_o)
conceptual assets.reasoning: The module derives availability and fullness indicators from empty/full/level (half <= level(...) or full at line 96; free <= not full at line 110; avail <= not empty at line 111) and exposes them on the output ports either directly (lines 217-219) or synchronized by sync_status (lines 247-256). The map shows free and avail DERIVES_FROM full/empty (occurrence 3 lines 110-111), half is GATED_BY level/full (occurrence 2 line 96), and the ports copy those signals (free_o / avail_o / half_o COPIES at occurrence 2 lines 217-219). The RTL therefore establishes integrity requirements for these status values because they are produced here and exported to consumers.

conceptual assets.concept: Clear command (clear_i) that forces next-pointer values to zero and thereby clears FIFO pointer state
conceptual assets.reasoning: The RTL explicitly assigns w_nxt and r_nxt to zero when clear_i = '1' (lines 82-83); pointer_reg then captures w_nxt/r_nxt on the next clock (lines 76-77), which clears the FIFO's head/tail state. The map records clear_i gating those next-pointer assignments (clear_i GATES w_nxt at occurrence 2 line 82 and GATES r_nxt at occurrence 3 line 83). Because clear_i directly changes pointer state and thus which entries are live, its correctness is an established integrity property of the FIFO's operation.
